Hi Marta (and Eugene),

Thanks — good questions and a common gotcha. Short answers up front: 1) We treat the audit period as inclusive of the vendor-stated end date (2026-06-14) using UTC-normalized timestamps for evidence collection; 2) For records where a customer-visible local timestamp differs from the canonical UTC event timestamp, our manifest maps evidence to the UTC timestamp used by our forensic snapshot.

Details: 
- Redwood's Type II evidence pipeline normalizes all event timestamps to UTC at ingestion for the purposes of the auditor bundle. The auditor's "inclusive end date" is applied to the UTC-normalized timestamp. That means an event whose recorded UTC time is on or before 2026-06-14T23:59:59Z will be considered in-period.
- Events that translate to 2026-06-15T06:47:31Z UTC (as in your example) would be outside the stated inclusive end date and therefore excluded from the Type II bundle. If customer-facing local time is inside the period but canonical UTC falls outside, we'll flag it in the manifest and exclude it unless you request an extended bridge period.
- For the bridge letter: Redwood issues a bridge letter tied to the vendor's stated audit period (the canonical period reported on the SOC 2) and then separately provides a point-in-time snapshot timestamp that was used to collect each evidence artifact. The bridge letter will explicitly state the cutoff we used for evidence inclusion and whether any compensating controls or exceptional inclusions were applied.

I'm attaching a small evidence manifest extract and a bridge-letter request template so your auditors have the fields they need (object id, artifact type, canonical UTC timestamp, snapshot source).

Let me know if you'd like us to run a quick filter for the Acme tenant and surface the specific objects that fall on the boundary — happy to do that and share a filtered CSV.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
